reviews.quote: As convertible Chromebooks go, the HP Chromebook Plus x360 falls short of the premium Acer Spin 714, but it costs a few hundred dollars less - a first-rate 2-in-1 alternative.
By and large it delivered exactly what I was expecting, with a standout 360-degree screen, quality webcam, and great value.

praises: 360° flip hinge + touch at $649.99 — the cheapest real convertible Chromebook Plus in CA retail
512GB SSD is the most storage on any N355 Chromebook listed, and NVMe (not eMMC)
2K WUXGA 16:10 touch panel is sharper and taller than the 16:9 FHD rivals
5MP webcam is far ahead of the 720p/1080p cams elsewhere in the class
HP's spill-resistant keyboard and convertible build suit classrooms and kitchens
complaints: No active pen support despite being a flip — tablet mode is finger-only
N355 is the same web-class CPU as the $450 Lenovo; you pay for the hinge, not speed
Convertibles flex more at the hinge than clamshells in this price class
$899.99 regular is bad value; only the $649.99 sale is competitive
ChromeOS tablet mode is shallow — few Android apps use the touch form factor well

standouts: Best convertible value in the inventory: 512GB NVMe + 2K touch + 5MP cam + flip hinge at $649.99 sale
design_philosophy: HP's Flip applies the Chromebook Plus formula to the 2-in-1 form: a 360° hinge and touch layer turn the same efficient N355 platform into a tablet/kiosk/stand machine, and HP loads this tier with the practical extras (512GB NVMe, 5MP camera, spill-resistant deck) that families actually use. The convertible is the one hardware dimension a Chromebook can gain without needing desktop apps.
